title: liveSwitch deploy pruning MAPPED (input_scenario_map) path silently selects the wrong live branch when two upstream labels collide under _sanitize_func_name (order-dependent, no ambiguity guard)
description: When a liveSwitch node DOES have an input_scenario_map with a 'live' entry, _live_only_edges resolves the live edge by scanning the switch's incoming edges and taking the FIRST whose source label sanitizes to live_input_name (lines 59-64), then `break`s. The guard at lines 65-69 only raises when NO edge matches. It does NOT detect the case where TWO distinct upstream source nodes have labels that collide under _sanitize_func_name (e.g. 'Live Source' and 'Live-Source' both -> 'Live_Source', since sanitize maps both space and hyphen to '_'). In that case both edges 'match' live_input_name; whichever edge is listed first in graph.edges wins, the other live-candidate is dropped, and prune_for_deploy returns normally with NO error. The deployed scoring path therefore depends on edge ordering and can keep the WRONG upstream branch. This is the inverse of the already-known fallback finding: the known finding (bucket 'known', verdict refuted) asserts the mapped path is the safe one that 'raises on no-match/collision, unlike the fallback' — this finding shows the mapped path is ALSO silently order-dependent on COLLISION (it only raises on no-match, not on ambiguous-match). It is also distinct from the codegen B3 finding, which concerns two input_scenario_map keys both mapped to 'live' (duplicate map VALUES); here the map has a single 'live' key but two SOURCE LABELS collide after sanitization.
evidence: Executed repro (temp script, project root sandboxed, then deleted). Graph: nodes a='Live Source'(dataSource), b='Live-Source'(dataSource) [both sanitize to 'Live_Source'], switch=liveSwitch config={input_scenario_map:{'Live_Source':'live','Other':'batch'}, inputs:['Live_Source','Other']}, output. Edges to switch ordered (a,b) vs (b,a). prune_for_deploy(graph,'output') returned with NO exception in both cases; surviving switch parent = {'a'} for order (a,b) and {'b'} for order (b,a). So the kept live branch flips with edge order and exactly one colliding source is silently chosen. Code trace: line 60 `if e.target == sid`; line 62 `if _sanitize_func_name(src_label) == live_input_name`; line 63 sets switch_live_source[sid]=e.source; line 64 `break` -> first-match-wins; the line 65 `if sid not in switch_live_source` guard never fires because a (colliding) match was found.
